texts.preamble: Reserved On : 02.07.2024 vs State Of Himachal Pradesh & Ors on 22 October, 2024 Author: Virender Singh Bench: Virender Singh 2024:Hhc:10106 In The High Court Of Himachal Pradesh, Shimla Cr.MMO No. : 834 of 2022 Reserved on : 02.07.2024 Decided on : 22.10.2024 T. Banambar Patra ...Petitioner Versus State of Himachal Pradesh & Ors. .......Respondents Coram The Hon'ble Mr. Justice Virender Singh, Judge.
texts.facts: 3. The present petition has been filed, on the ground that M/s T.K. International Ltd. is a company, registered under the Companies Act and is dealing with the hotel business, throughout the country. The petitioner is the Managing Director of the said firm. 3.1 M/s T.K. International Ltd. is having its one unit i.e. Resort at Shilon Bagh, District Shimla, H.P., whereas, respondent No.1, through Food Inspector, Shimla, has instituted a complaint, under Section 16(1)(a)(I) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (hereinafter referred to as the 'Act'), which is pending adjudication, before the learned trial Court. Reserved On : 02.07.2024 vs State Of Himachal Pradesh & Ors on 22 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76058015/ 1 2024:HHC:10106 3.2 According to the petitioner, when, he came to know about the passing of the summoning orders against him, then, he had challenged the order dated 02.06.2010, 23.05.2011 and 30.06.2011, by preferring Criminal Revision Petition No.29-S/10 of 2011, before the learned Sessions Judge, Shimla, however, the same was dismissed on 12.09.2011. 3.3 It is the case of the petitioner that the order dated 12.09.2011, passed by the learned Sessions Judge, Shimla, was assailed, before this Court, by way of Cr.MMO No.189 of 2011 and vide judgment dated 01.07.2014, the said petition was allowed by quashing the orders dated 02.06.2010, 23.05.2011 and 30.06.2011. 3.4 Despite this fact, according to the petitioner, the learned trial Court has again issued the summons. The petitioner also came to know about the fact that order dated 03.09.2015 and subsequent orders, passed by the learned trial Court, were passed on the similar facts and complaint, without application of judicial mind. 3.5 It is the further case of the petitioner that thereafter, he has assailed the orders dated 03.09.2015, 30.09.2015, 27.10.2015, 27.11.2015, 24.12.2015, 2024:HHC:10106 12.01.2018, 30.05.2018, 23.06.2018, 30.07.2018, 07.09.2018 and subsequent orders, by way of Cr.MMO No.544 of 2018. However, the said case was dismissed, by this Court, vide judgment dated 03.12.2019. 3.6 Thereafter, the matter was listed, before the learned trial Court, on 19.12.2019, when, the petitioner was duly represented by his counsel and the learned trial Court, without putting notice of accusation to the accused (petitioner), has fixed the case for complainant's evidence. 3.7 Later, on account of COVID-19 pandemic w.e.f. 24.03.2020, proceedings of the Court were affected and due to the restrictions, so imposed, one of the unit of M/s T.K. International Ltd. and its resort, was closed down completely. The petitioner, being the Managing Director of the said firm, came to know through the officials of M/s Toshali Resort/accused No.2, in the second week of May, 2022, that some process, issued by the learned trial Court, has been affixed in the building of M/s Toshali Resort/accused No.2. The said process was ordered to be served through nominee/Director of M/s Toshali Resort/accused No.2. 2024 : HHC:10106 4. All these facts have been highlighted to demonstrate that there was no specific name of any nominee or Director in the said process. 5. It is the further case of the petitioner that thereafter, the Managing Director of M/s T.K. International Ltd. appointed its authorized representative and later, it was found that accused No.2 has been declared proclaimed offender vide order dated 19.04.2022. Subsequently, application for recalling the said order was moved on 19.04.2022. 5.1 Vide order dated 06.08.2022, the learned trial Court allowed the said application and issued the non-bailable warrants against accused No.2, through its Managing Director (petitioner), for 12.09.2022. 5.2 The order dated 06.08.2022 has been impugned, before this Court, on the ground that the said order is perverse and non-speaking. According to the petitioner, in pursuance of order dated 31.10.2011, the notice of accusation was put to accused, but, vide judgment, passed by this Court, on 01.07.2014 in Cr.MMO No.189 of 2011, the orders including cognizance order, passed by the learned trial Court, were [LEAKAGE_MASK]. As such, 2024:HHC:10106 there is no notice of accusation, against the petitioner, as on date. Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76058015/ 2 5.3 It is the further case of the petitioner that although bail bonds and personal bonds were furnished, in terms of the order dated 17.10.2011, but, in view of the judgment dated 01.07.2014, passed by this Court, the bail bonds and personal bonds were discharged and subsequently, no bonds were executed. 6. These facts have been highlighted to show that the order, by virtue of which, the proceedings, under Section 446 of CrPC, were initiated, is nonest and unsustainable in the eyes of law. 7. As per the petitioner, although, the application for recalling the order dated 19.04.2022 was allowed, by the learned trial Court, but, non-bailable warrants were issued against the petitioner, highlighting the fact that the company i.e. M/s T.K. International Ltd., registered, under the Companies Act, is dealing with the hotel business, throughout the country and respondent No.2-M/s Toshali View Resort is one of its units. 7.1 Another ground, upon which, the quashing of order, impugned herein, has been sought, is that at the 2024:HHC:10106 relevant time, when, the sample was collected by the complainant, one Sh. Saswat Patra was the Manager of M/s Toshali View Resort, whereas, accused No.1 was posted as Assistant Restaurant Manager and was dealing with food articles, in the restaurant. Similarly, the order, by virtue of which, the bail bonds were ordered to be forfeited to the State of Himachal Pradesh and proceedings, under Section 446 of CrPC, were initiated, is also stated to be bad in law. 7.3 In addition to this, according to the petitioner, respondent No.2/accused was In-charge of the restaurant, who has been declared proclaimed offender, vide order dated 02.06.2010. Respondent No.2 was being represented by its Manager, before the learned trial Court and appeared on various dates. The complaint is also stated to be barred by limitation, as per provisions of Section 473 of CrPC. 2024:HHC:10106 8. On the basis of above facts, a prayer has been made to allow the petition, as prayed for. No reasons were assigned by the trial Court. 11. Order dated 03.09.2015, passed by the learned trial Court, has been challenged by petitioner-T. Banambar Patra, by way of petition, bearing Cr.MMO No.544 of 2018. The said petition was dismissed, by this Court, on 03.12.2019. 13. In the complaint, Mr. Joginder Boipoi has been arrayed as accused No.1 and M/s Toshali Resort, through 2024:HHC:10106 its nominee/Managing Director, has been arrayed as accused No.2. 14. 15. In order to secure the presence of accused, non- bailable warrants were issued against accused Joginder Boipoi and thereafter, the proclamation, under Section 82 of CrPC, was issued against him, on 19.11.2018, for 29.12.2018. 15.1 In the meantime, petitioner-T. Banambar Patra had filed Cr.MMO No.544 of 2018, seeking quashing of order dated 03.09.2015 and subsequent orders, passed by the learned trial Court. Ultimately, the said petition was dismissed, by this Court, on 03.12.2019. Record reveals that in the present case the notice of accusation has already been framed against the accused No.2 namely T.B. Patra on 31.10.2011. Therefore, list the case for CW's. Let CW's be summoned through special messenger returnable for 25.02.2020." 2024:HHC:10106 18. After passing the order dated 03.09.2015, by the learned trial Court, the process was issued to secure the presence of the accused persons, namely Joginder Boipoi, who has been mentioned as Assistant Manager of M/s Toshali Resort, and Managing Director of M/s Toshali Resort, Shilon Bagh. When, the bailable warrants, issued by the learned trial Court, could not be executed, then, on 12.01.2018, non-bailable warrants were ordered to be issued, by the learned trial Court, against the accused persons, by passing the following order:- "BW to the issued could not be issued for want of CA. However, Food Inspector has submitted that the address as mentioned in the complaint is actual address of the accused No.2. It has been submitted that the accused persons are deliberately trying to evade the service of this court. From the perusal of record, it is evident that despite issuance of summons/BWs, service of the accused persons could not be effect by this court. The present matter is urgent and targeted in nature. Therefore, let NBW be now issued against the accused on the address that has been mentioned in complaint as well as authorized representative/nominee of accused No.2 to be executed through special messenger not below the rank of ASI under the intimation of Deputy S.P. Concerned returnable for 21.02.2018. Reserved On : 02.07.2024 vs State Of Himachal Pradesh & Ors on 22 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76058015/ 5 19. A perusal of record shows that in this case, on 12.01.2010, the Food Inspector had submitted an 2024:HHC:10106 application by mentioning the correct address of accused No.2, as 'Sh. T. Banambar Patra, Managing Director of Toshali Resorts International Toshali House, Y-42/4 Shahtoot Marg DLF Phase-1, Qutab Enclave Gurgaon- 122002', whereas, in the complaint, filed before the learned trial Court, name of T. Banambar Patra has not been mentioned. In the complaint, the description of accused No.2 has been mentioned, as 'M/s Toshali Resort Shilon Bag Shimla, through its Nominee/Managing Director'. No document has been placed on record, which would show that petitioner-T. Banambar Patra is the Managing Director of M/s Toshali Resort. 20. Thereafter, the proceedings, under Section 82 of CrPC, were initiated against the accused. After dismissal of Cr.MMO No.544 of 2018, on 03.12.2019, the learned trial Court had listed the matter for CWs, on the basis of the notice of accusation, which was put to the accused, on 31.10.2011. It is not in dispute that the summoning order dated 23.12.2009 was [LEAKAGE_MASK] by this Court on 01.07.2014. He had furnished the requisite bail bonds and thereafter, notice of accusation was put to him on 31.10.2011. The summoning order dated 23.12.2009 has admittedly been [LEAKAGE_MASK] on 01.07.2014. Meaning thereby, whatsoever act, done by the Court, in pursuance of the said summoning order, does not survive, thereafter. 22. Although, on 03.09.2015, the process was again issued and when, the presence of the accused persons could not be secured, then, the proceedings, under Section 82 CrPC, were initiated and on 29.12.2018, the proclamation, so issued, was received back duly executed. However, no formal order to declare the accused as proclaimed offenders has been passed. Subsequently, the matter was again taken up on 19.12.2019, when, the file was received by the learned trial Court, after dismissal of Cr.MMO No.544 of 2018, on 03.12.2019. After passing the summoning order dated 03.09.2015, there is nothing on file to show that accused T. Banambar Patra was directed to furnish any bail or surety bond. 2024:HHC:10106 23. The order, impugned herein, is liable to be [LEAKAGE_MASK] on the ground that the learned trial Court, on the basis of notice of accusation, dated 31.10.2011, had listed the matter for CWs, whereas, the fresh notice of accusation was required to be put to the accused after setting aside the summoning order dated 03.09.2015. 24. 25. By way of the present petition, order dated 06.08.2022 has also been assailed.
texts.arguments: Relevant paragraphs 6 and 7 of the said judgment, are reproduced, as under:- "6. As per Section 17(2) every person whosoever at the time of the offence was in charge of, and was responsible to, the company for the conduct of the business of the company is liable until and unless he proves in the Court that offence was committed without his knowledge. Learned counsel, appearing for petitioner-T. Banambar Patra, has rightly pointed out that on this score alone, the present petition is liable to be allowed, as, notice of accusation has not been put to the accused, on the basis of the summoning order, which was passed on 03.09.2015. 26. Learned Additional Advocate General, appearing for respondent No.1, could not satisfy the judicial conscience of this Court, as to when the summoning order 2024:HHC:10106 dated 23.12.2009 was [LEAKAGE_MASK] by this Court, then, how the bail/surety bonds, so furnished, on 17.10.2011, could be forfeited, after passing the fresh summoning order dated 03.09.2015, as, no bail/surety bonds were ever furnished by accused T. Banambar Patra, in pursuance of the order dated 03.09.2015. 27. In this case, a futile attempt has also been made by learned counsel for the petitioner by arguing that not only the order, impugned herein, but, the entire proceedings, initiated against the accused, are abuse of the process of law and as such, the same are liable to be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. 2024:HHC:10106 (m) That in the fact of the case, vague, unlawful, defective process adopted, conclusion reached in proceeding against the petitioner which is bad in law, unsustainable and against law and has led to travesty of justice." 28. Per contra, learned Additional Advocate General has rightly pointed out that on account of dismissal of Cr.MMO No.544 of 2018, on 03.12.2019, by this Court, the said prayer is not sustainable in the eyes of law, as, the order dated 03.09.2015, by virtue of which, the summoning order was passed against the accused, was challenged unsuccessfully. 28.1. To buttress his contention, learned Additional Advocate General has relied upon para 3 of the judgment, passed by the Coordinate Bench of this Court, in Cr.MMO No.544 of 2018, which is reproduced, as under:- Reserved On : 02.07.2024 vs State Of Himachal Pradesh & Ors on 22 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76058015/ 7 "3. Mr. C.N. Singh, learned counsel for the petitioner has argued that the summoning order issued by the learned Magistrate earlier was [LEAKAGE_MASK] by this Court and now in the same fashion the present summoning order has been issued, which is also required to be [LEAKAGE_MASK], since the petitioner is Managing Director of the Company and no order can be passed against him, until and unless the Magistrate for the reasons comes to the conclusion that act is done under his supervision. Learned counsel for the petitioner has brought the attention of this Court to the orders passed by learned Magistrate from time to time, as well as the judgments (Annexures P-2 and P-4) passed by this Court. He has also cited the law settled in Mr. T.K. Sibal & others 2024:HHC:10106 of 2012, decided on 21.05.2018 and argued that since this Court has already held in Cr. MMO No. 190 of 2011 that the summoning orders were passed without application of mind, the present petition may be allowed and impugned order dated 03.09.2015 alongwith subsequent orders may be [LEAKAGE_MASK] and [LEAKAGE_MASK]." 29. These facts have been highlighted by the learned Additional Advocate General to demonstrate that once, Cr.MMO has been dismissed by a Coordinate Bench of this Court, then, the said order cannot be reviewed by this Court. The said arguments of learned Additional Advocate General hold water, as the petitioner (accused) has already taken similar grounds to assail the order dated 03.09.2015 and with the dismissal of the said petition, this Court cannot exercise the powers, under Section 482 of CrPC, to nullify the findings, recorded by the Coordinate Bench, in Cr.MMO No.544 of 2018.
